chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
When you rise from your sleep at night, say: All praise is for Allah, who returned my soul to me so that I may thank Him and worship Him.

When you hear the crowing of the roosters, say: Pure, Holy, our Lord and Lord of the angels and the Spirit. Your mercy precedes Your wrath. There is no god but You alone, no partner for You. I did evil and wronged myself, so forgive me and have mercy on me, for it is You who forgives sins.

When you rise, look at the horizons of the sky and say: O Allah, a dark night does not hide from You, nor a sky with its towers, nor an earth with its resting places, nor darknesses one upon another, nor a deep sea that precedes the one who precedes from Your creation. You know the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal. The stars have set, the eyes have slept, and You are the Ever-Living, the Sustainer, whom neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes. Pure is Allah, Lord of the worlds, and God of the Messengers. And all praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds.
Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth
Then recite the five verses from Surah Al-Imran, from 'Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth' to His saying: 'Indeed, You do not fail in Your promise.'

Then rinse your mouth and perform ablution. When you place your hand in the water, say: In the name of Allah and by Allah. O Allah, make me among those who repent and make me among those who purify themselves. When you finish, say: All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds.

When you stand for your prayer, say: In the name of Allah and by Allah, and to Allah and from Allah, and what Allah willed. No power and no strength except with Allah. O Allah, make me among Your visitors and builders of Your mosques. Open for me, O Lord, the door of Your repentance, and close from me the door of my disobedience and all disobedience. All praise is for Allah who made me among those who converse with Him.
Turn Your face toward me, O Exalted in praise. Then commence the prayer with the Takbir.
The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Then he rises to his place of prayer, up to the phrase 'and it is recommended that he make du'a (qunut) with this supplication.'
ai.seo_question: What are the recommended supplications and rituals when waking up for night prayer in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Attributed to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) and recorded in al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith provides a comprehensive ritual guide for Tahajjud, emphasizing the transition from sleep to worship through specific dhikr and Quranic recitation. It highlights the scholarly tradition of integrating cosmic awareness—referencing the night sky and stars—with personal accountability before commencing ablution and prayer. The inclusion of specific verses from Surah Al-Imran underscores the theological link between divine promise-keeping and the believer’s devotion during night vigils.
